questions.prompt: What does a TypeScript type assertion do?
options: It inserts a runtime validator for every field.
It changes the JavaScript value into a different object.
It guarantees the asserted type is correct.
It tells the compiler to treat an expression as a type; it does not validate the value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: It tells the compiler to treat an expression as a type; it does not validate the value at runtime.
questions.explanation: Use an assertion only when independent evidence justifies it; validation is separate.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Assertion Functions”?
options: A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with assertion signatures and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with assertion signatures and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Assertion signatures”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Assertion Functions”?
options: Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
Check runtime checks paired with type narrowing, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume appropriate use in validation utilities is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
questions.answer_key: Check runtime checks paired with type narrowing, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Runtime checks paired with type narrowing”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
